02 / 12
The problem

More telemetry
≠ more understanding.

Metrics+Logs+Traces+Profiles+Events+Kubernetes+Cloud

We have more visibility than ever. The challenge is finding the signal and connecting it to the failure.

Telemetry gives us data.
It doesn't automatically give us understanding.
03 / 12
Four different questions

These are not the same thing.

ConceptQuestionExample
MonitoringIs something wrong?P99 latency > 2s
ObservabilityWhat is happening?Checkout → payment is slow
DebuggabilityCan I figure out why?Only version v42 is affected
CausalityWhat caused it?Pool change → DB exhaustion → queueing
04 / 12
Monitoring

Monitoring answers:
“Should I care?”

Signal→Threshold→Alert→Human

Monitoring is excellent at detecting known failure conditions: latency, error rate, saturation, availability.

Monitoring tells you that something is wrong.
05 / 12
Observability

Observability answers:
“What is happening?”

Metrics

What changed?

Logs

What happened?

Traces

Where did the request go?

Client
  ↓
API
  ↓
Checkout
  ↓
Payment
  ↓
Database

But which component actually caused the latency?

Good observability reduces search.
Good debuggability reduces time to hypothesis.

07 / 12
Causality

Correlation is not causality.

DB latency ↑
    ↓
Connection pool saturation
    ↓
Request queue grows
    ↓
API latency ↑
    ↓
Timeouts ↑
    ↓
Retries ↑
    ↓
CPU ↑

The first metric to move isn't necessarily the root cause.

08 / 12
Design for debuggability

Give engineers the context to converge.

What changed?Deployments · config · feature flags · infrastructure
What is affected?Service · version · region · cluster · tenant
Where is the failure?Dependency graph · trace · network path
What can I do?Runbook · rollback · safe remediation · automation

Often this isn't about collecting new telemetry. It's about connecting information we already have.

09 / 12
What should we measure?

Maybe our KPI isn't
telemetry coverage.

⏳ Time to Understand

How quickly can an engineer explain what happened?

Alert → hypothesisHypothesis → confirmationMTTR% incidents with known cause% requiring another team
10 / 12
A simplified example

Checkout latency incident

10:02Alert: P99 latency > 2s
10:05Traces show checkout → payment slow
10:08Only version v42 affected
10:12Recent change: connection pool size
10:15DB connections exhausted
10:18Rollback v42
10:20Latency back to normal

The win isn't “more telemetry.”
It's getting to the causal story faster.

11 / 12
The takeaway

Don't just make systems observable.

Monitoring
Detect→Observability
Explore→Debuggability
Understand→Causality
Explain→Automation
Act
The goal isn't to collect more telemetry.
The goal is to make failures easy to understand.

Final question: If an engineer joins your on-call rotation tomorrow, can they actually debug your system?
